🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Tommy Walsh, the television presenter and celebrity builder who became a household name on the BBC's garden makeover show Ground Force, has died at 69.

Walsh died on Sunday, November 9, 2026, after a long illness, his agent Debbie Schiesser confirmed to the Press Association. "Tommy died peacefully after a long illness surrounded by his family," Schiesser said, asking that the family's privacy be respected.

Walsh was born on December 18, 1956, in Hackney, London, and worked as a builder by trade. He first came to public attention in 1997, when he joined the BBC's Ground Force after doing building work at the home of the show's executive producer, who invited him to a screen test. He handled the hard landscaping on the show, working alongside Alan Titchmarsh and Charlie Dimmock, and stayed with it for the rest of its run, until 2005. At its peak, Ground Force drew up to 12 million viewers, making it one of the biggest shows of its era.

After Ground Force, Walsh went on to present a string of home improvement shows, including Challenge Tommy Walsh, Homes Under the Hammer, Flip That House with Tommy Walsh and Clean It, Fix It.

Walsh had spoken openly about his health. He was diagnosed with throat cancer in 2022 and made a full recovery, and in January 2024 he revealed that doctors had found a tumour in his lung.

Rest in Peace, Tommy Walsh.

Sources: Press Association (statement from agent Debbie Schiesser, November 9, 2026); BBC; Radio Times.
